summary: Steel Arkansas Forestry Commission lookout, 40 ft (12.2 m) tall, on Goosepond Mountain in Saline County, described by federal surveyors in 1940. Present state not documented.

events.note: Described by the Coast and Geodetic Survey as an Arkansas Forestry Commission lookout tower on the highest point of Goosepond Mountain, 40 feet high

evidence.supports: Arkansas Forestry Commission set up 1931 and built many more towers
evidence.quote: The Arkansas Forestry Commission was established by Act 234 in 1931, and it too built many more towers.

evidence.supports: Saline County, about 14 miles NE of Hot Springs, lookout tower of the Arkansas Forestry Commission on the highest point
evidence.quote: STATION IS A LOOKOUT TOWER OF THE ARKANSAS FORESTRY COMMISSION, LOCATED ON THE HIGHEST POINT OF GOOSEPOND MOUNTAIN, ABOUT 14 MILES NE OF HOT SPRINGS.

evidence.supports: described 1940 by Coast and Geodetic Survey

THE TOWER IS OF STEEL CONSTRUCTION AND IS 40 FEET HIGH.

sources.title: NGS Data Sheet listing for PID EJ1897

notes_for_editor: No build date or present condition in any readable source. The NHLR and FFLOS caches do not list this tower. The NGS 1940 description gives 40 ft, which the brief lacked, so height_m 12.2 is added as a fact, not a correction. The 2023 Arkansas Democrat-Gazette fire-tower article is paywalled, and its cached text is only a stub, so it was not used. Coordinates in the brief match the NGS datasheet position (34 40 30 N, 092 54 36 W), so no correction is proposed.
